facts.claim: APP1 has a service path that forwards APP0 to the BMC. 0x8017D218 opens A:/SP404MKII_APP0.bin (string at 0x8023C375) or a service alternative A:/TD003_ROM.bin (0x8023C3B6). Worker 0x8017D2C0 reads 4096 bytes at a time into the non-cacheable buffer at 0x83FF0000 and passes each block on through a callback that ends at LPUART3. The resident updater has a separate path (app0.upd1-transfer).

In normal running, changing an effect sends a type number and parameters and no program load was found. 0x800D0CF0 sends TYPE, 0x801805D0-0x801806E2 sends starting parameters. What the second processor does after a TYPE message is unknown.

facts.claim: SP APP0 5.52 has an opaque 310160-byte block at file offsets 0x60 through 0x4BBEF. The App1_Main header names destination 0x01000000 and entry word 0x01000001, consistent with ARM Thumb code. The control word 0xB6020001 matches the verified 3DES mode and slot 0xB6 on MC-101 and SYSTEM-8. Both published parsers locate the block on SP, but the local decrypt runs ended for lack of compatible key material. ARM control code is the leading interpretation. The exact contents and SP cipher compatibility remain unverified. The open DSP catalogue is outside this block.

facts.claim: 383 MFX parameter records exist in APP1. Each parameter has a 20-byte descriptor at 0x8021996C + 20 x p: default, minimum, maximum, knob position within its effect, and a last word that is 1 for MFX. p is one index over all 627 descriptors of the firmware, shared with the formatters at 0x80218F9C + 4 x p and the names at 0x80245EE4 + 4 x p; the MFX descriptors are p = 163 (type 1, Filter+Drive) to 545, one run of knob positions per type, for example Compressor 383-387 and COMPRESSOR 2 388-393 (app0.comp2-params). Type names are at 0x8020B3D8 + 4 x ID. 0x8022E1C8 is a table of 54 entries of 6 bytes, three halfwords each (first record, last record, last record again), together covering p = 0-626: entries 0-3 are 0-32, 33-76, 77-122, 123-162, and MFX type t (1-48) is entry t+3, for example Compressor (28) = entry 31 (383, 387, 387) and COMPRESSOR 2 (29) = entry 32 (388, 393, 393) at 0x8022E288; entries 52-53 (546-581, 582-626) are not MFX. 0x8001D950 and 0x800D8118 walk it (9 entries per step of 0x36 bytes, to 0x144) and return the entry whose range holds a given p; what they use it for (perhaps building the DT1 address) is a hypothesis. The range and scaling of an effect knob do not come from the 20-byte descriptor: see app0.knob-ranges. Earlier text here named 0x8022E30C as the descriptor table: that is wrong; the records there have a different layout, whose role and total count are not established. Record index 44 at 0x8022E67C has words [0, 0, 1, 0x0021000B, 103]; a change in its last word does not establish the end of the table. Type selector values 126-130 pick the type for each slot. Reverb PLATE/MOD and Super Filter NOTCH name strings exist beyond their allowed ranges.

facts.claim: Type 29, COMPRESSOR 2 (app0.hidden-types), works on a unit. Chosen in the grid on BUS 1 (hk.recipe.mfx-grid-entry), the screen shows BUS 1 COMPRESSOR 2 with the knobs SUSTAIN, ATTACK and RATIO, and the knobs change the sound clearly. TONE across its whole range, -100 to 100, changes it very little. MODE = LIMIT silences everything on the bus. By ear it is harsher than the ordinary Compressor (28), and its settings act more strongly. It is not offered for BUS 3 or 4 in FX SETTING, which uses another list (st.mfx.other-lists). An earlier try, 2026-11-13, set only the type by a DT1 (hw.bmc.sysex) while the knobs went on sending the parameters of the effect chosen before: there a bass note through type 29 was identical, sample for sample, to the dry note. So with the parameters of another effect it changed nothing; with its own, sent by the stock grid, it works. Why LIMIT mutes the bus and why TONE does so little is not known: a property of this program, or of the parameter values the stock sends for it. Its parameter records and the DT1 a MODE turn sends: app0.comp2-params.

facts.claim: APP0 carries a CRC-32 that anyone can recompute: with length = the 32-bit little-endian word at file offset 0x44, the word at 0x60 + length + 12 equals the standard CRC-32 (zlib) of every byte before it, that is the header, the closed block and the 12 bytes after it. It holds in all five known versions (3.02, 4.04, 5.01, 5.50, 5.52). The open effect programs further on in the file lie outside this sum; whether anything else checks them is not known. The header word at 0x50 is a different value whose meaning is not established.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: five APP0 files: the stored word against zlib.crc32, computed twice by two agents independently; in 5.52 the word is at 0x4BBFC and reads 0x1A05DABA

facts.claim: The APP0 catalogue at file offset 0x15D698 holds, for each type number 0-48, two pointers: the effect's program for the second processor and its memory block. The pointers are file offset + 0xC0000. Each points at a descriptor of four words: 0, size, the same size again, and the address of the bytes. In APP0 5.52 four pairs of types share both program and memory block byte for byte: 0 Bypass and 45 Sub Sonic, 10 Reverb and 37 Ha-Dou, 12 Resonator and 35 Hyper-Reso, 24 Stopper and 38 To-Gu-Ro. So within a pair the difference likely comes from elsewhere, from the parameters APP1 sends or from tables outside the catalogue; not checked. 28 Compressor and 29 COMPRESSOR 2 are different programs, 796 and 746 bytes, with memory blocks of 40 bytes each. Bypass is 66 bytes.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: SP404MKII_APP0.bin from the Roland 5.52 update package, SHA256 3e35ff30137f741a715566e205384f9b434ca7ac3847e247bad3f0c9c8a2bd23: all 98 catalogue pointers followed and the blocks compared, 2026-11-13, recomputed in this repository the same day

facts.claim: Parameters of the two compressors in the descriptor table 0x8021996C (app0.params): Compressor (28) is records 383 SUSTAIN, 384 ATTACK, 385 LEVEL, 386 RATIO, 387 MODE; COMPRESSOR 2 (29) is records 388 SUSTAIN, 389 ATTACK, 390 LEVEL, 391 RATIO, 392 TONE (shown -100 to 100), 393 MODE. The knob table 0x802E5B40 + 24 x type (app0.knob-ranges) puts them on the controls as 388, 389, 391, 390, 392, 393 for type 29 (so RATIO before LEVEL) and 383, 384, 386, 385, none, none for type 28, so Compressor's MODE has no control there. Both MODEs are 0-1, shown COMP or LIMIT through a value-name list at 0x80244530. Record 393 at 0x8021B820 reads default 0, min 0, max 1 (the word at 0x8021B828), knob 5, 1. Turning MODE on the effect page sends DT1 address 03 01 0D 0A with value 00 01 for BUS 1 (type 29, knob 5 = LIMIT) and 03 01 0E 0A for BUS 2, as hw.bmc.sysex predicts. Path of a knob on the effect page: 0x80147B84 -> 0x800DE270 -> range from 0x800D3260 and scaling 0x800D1188 -> 0x80018B90 -> sender 0x800D93F0. Both 0x800D3260 and 0x800D1188 take max and min from the second tables 0x801AC830 and 0x801AD1FC (app0.knob-ranges), not from the descriptor; for p = 393 that max is the word 0x801ACE54 = 1. So pinning MODE to COMP is not just setting 0x8021B828 to 0: 0x801ACE54 holds the max that knob turns use. No such change has been tested, on the emulator or a unit, and what the stock then does with a project that saved LIMIT is not checked. On the DM-404 emulator the second page of the COMPRESSOR 2 controls (TONE, MODE) could not be opened: on the BUS 1 effect page, turning VALUE and pressing MFX again showed the BPM screen, and SHIFT+CTRL1-3 turned parameters 1-3. How a unit reaches MODE was not recorded. Later (2026-11-18): the second page opens by holding VALUE and turning a CTRL (st.efx.knob-pages). With both maxima of p = 393 set to 0 (0x8021B828 and 0x801ACE54) MODE stayed COMP over the whole travel of its knob on the emulator, on the effect page and in EFX SET BUS 3/4, where the unchanged firmware reaches LIMIT with CTRL3; the cell itself still shows MODE COMP, and on the owner's unit the cell was seen in EFX SET. Whether a unit can still reach LIMIT with that change, and what a project that saved LIMIT does, is not reported.

facts.claim: Effect knobs take their range from two tables of 627 words beside the descriptors of app0.params: max at 0x801AC830 + 4 x p and min at 0x801AD1FC + 4 x p (for p = 383-395 max 255, 255, 255, 255, 1, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 1, 9, 9 and min all 0, the same values as the descriptor max and min there). The range function 0x800D3260 and the scaling 0x800D1188 read them for controls 0x27F-0x284 (639-644, the six effect controls): p comes from 0x802E5B40 + 24 x type + 4 x (control - 639), the type being a halfword at offset 0xC4 + 2 x slot of the state passed in; -1 means no parameter. 0x800D1188 maps a position 0-255 to min + (max - min + 1) x position / 255 (rounded); for control 0x57 it uses the entries at p = 87; for other controls it returns the value unchanged. Whether anything else still reads the descriptor max (0x8021996C + 20 x p + 8) for MFX, and which of the two wins on screen or when a project loads, is not established; a change to only one of them is untested; a change to both for p = 393 is recorded in app0.comp2-params.

facts.claim: SP 5.52 APP0 shares 2839, 1708, 2995 and 3030 distinct aligned ciphertext words with the 1.82 MC-101, MC-707 and MV-1 C0A and SYSTEM-8 1.32 C0A respectively. Shifting the reference grid one byte yields zero matches for every device. All five contain a common 696-byte sequence with 86 distinct eight-byte words. Using known plaintext from the MC-101 1.82 patch manifest identifies 370 zero words in SP, or 2960 bytes. None of the nonzero manifest words mapped into SP. Actual SP plaintext code remains unavailable.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: 2026-11-25, stock SP 5.52, MC-101, MC-707 and VERSELAB MV-1 1.82 and SYSTEM-8 1.32. Input hashes, cross-model offsets and exact method in knowledge/notes/APP0_DECRYPTION_REPORT.md.

facts.claim: In the five examined stock SP versions, the APP1 encoder's 12-byte parameter map has five records per non-Bypass MFX type. Its APP0 copy matches APP1 in 4.04 through 5.52. In 3.02 only the five type-16 rows differ, with range sizes 16 in APP1 and 18 in APP0. Type 48 changes from size 2 to 22 in both maps in 4.04, matching one to eleven APP1 parameters. Type 49's five records disappear. Type 45 has size 2 in all five versions. The BMC's use of the map and the meaning of the 3.02 runtime discrepancy have not been observed.

evidence.label: BYTES

facts.claim: Immediately after the open APP0 parameter map and 20 zero bytes are groups of 38 to 40 odd values in the declared load interval of the closed block. Two zero words separate consecutive groups. There are 49 groups in stock 3.02 and 48 in 4.04 through 5.52, matching the counts of non-Bypass MFX types. The values are consistent with Thumb function pointers. The dispatch order and the handler implementing MFX selection remain unverified.

facts.claim: In the SP UPD1 1.10 dump, the standard APP0 path marks a file FOUND when it opens, uses its length for the progress count, and sends the file in 4096-byte blocks on BMC requests. The traced host path performs no APP0 content or fixed-length check. It displays APP0 UPDATER OK on the BMC completion reply, without an independent host readback or reboot. UPD0 validation, flash write order and recovery remain unknown. See hw.boot.loader-image for the dump identifier and docs/SAFETY.md for recovery limits.

facts.claim: Between stock SP 3.02 and 4.04, type 48 changed from the Bypass duplicate Torcido (66-byte program, 8-byte companion and one APP1 parameter) to DJFX Delay (1398-byte program, 48-byte companion and 11 APP1 parameters). Types 0 through 47 kept the same payloads, and the trailing Bypass duplicate type 49 disappeared. The first shared DSP4 program grew from 1122 to 1140 bytes and the closed payload changed. The comparison establishes the paired APP1 and APP0 changes and leaves the dependencies of the new MFX and the BMC acceptance rules open.

facts.claim: A read-only 5.52 experiment replaced catalogue type 45 in the reference model with an original 72-byte framed saturation program, leaving its eight-byte companion and the other 48 entries unchanged. The test selected the entry by index and verified both output pairs for 49 stereo inputs before and after the replacement. DSP loading and update acceptance on SP remain unverified.
